schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE SYSTEM DEVICE — the one device that stands in for the host underneath, and the OWNER OF THE HOST READING (CPU, memory, disk). It samples the host and serves that reading; the OS-specific backing (load average vs a richer sampler; and, in the same family, privilege via sudo_relay) swaps behind it. It owns the reading and NOTHING ELSE. It is not a central scheduler, and — RULED 2026-08-04 — it is not a broker for other devices' predicates either: a device that wants a line on a host resource declares its own Probe with that line in its trigger, and ITS OWN SHIM fires it. `SystemRackmountDevice` subclasses `BaseDevice` (CP1-CP6, Form v0 #2); `SystemRackmountShim` subclasses `BaseShim` for the probes this device declares FOR ITSELF.
why: Because the host is genuinely ONE thing, so its reading has one owner (Law 6) and one place the OS-specific mess is contained — but a PREDICATE is not a reading. A line is chosen by the device that cares, for that device's own reason, and it belongs where the reason is: 'each device should own its own everything as much as possible, that's encapsulation' (Akien, 2026-08-04). The old shape had this device holding a menu, a subscription table, and a resolve-my-own-method indirection so other devices could keep their predicates HERE — a second firing path running parallel to the one every shim already has, justified by a Law 6 claim ('the raw reading never leaves') that was never Law 6 at all: Law 6 gates WRITES. What survives from the old why is real and small: no device is coupled to the OS, because the sampler is here. What dies is the protocol around it. This still corrects the original goof (the rackmount is NOT the rack — the rack is the chassis: bus + shims) and still is not a scheduler.
invoke: Construct: `dev = SystemRackmountDevice(sampler=None)` (inject a sampler in proofs). Inspect offerings: `dev.advertises()`. Subscribe: `dev.subscribe('cpu_threshold', address='ops/personal', why=..., value=80)` → a subscription id. Wire it to the beat: `shim = SystemRackmountShim(dev, bus); ground_loop.subscribe(shim)` — the shim pokes subscribers whose line is crossed on each `beat`. Prove: `python3 cairn/system_rackmount/proofs/test_system_rackmount.py` (exit 0 = green). Prove the diagnostic producer (bare, no bus): `python3 cairn/system_rackmount/proofs/test_diagnostic_emit.py`.
node_class: device — a rack-mount device on the spine (the spine step after ground_loop). It is the owner of the host's resource predicates; it serves threshold probes on them through the universal heartbeat + shim + bus mechanism.
entry: FRESH design to Form v0. The METAPHOR is quarried from UU (a rack holds rack-mount devices; a bus connects them; system services are abstracted so devices are portable), but the shape is Cairn's: a BaseDevice that OWNS host-resource data and ADVERTISES probes on it, resolving its own method so a caller stays ignorant of internals, and poking through the shared heartbeat + bus rather than a bespoke scheduler. What is NEW and Cairn's: advertise → subscribe → poke as the registration protocol; Law-6-local-evaluation (the host metric never leaves the device); the system device as a data-OWNER, not a service-registry or scheduler.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
red: THIS COMPONENT IS RED (Law 9), 2026-08-04. The spec above changed by ruling; the CODE still ships the broker — ADVERTISED, subscribe(), _resolve(), the _subs table, subscription_probes(), and the capstone proof that seals all of it. Named here rather than left for the next reader to trip over, because a charter that no longer describes its code is the drift Law 5 exists to make impossible. It goes green when the broker is gone and a consumer device fires its own host predicate through its own shim. → ticket owed: the-shim-fires-its-own-host-predicate
filed_edges: (a) SUPERSEDED 2026-08-04 — this edge ('memory/disk predicates are the SAME shape and mount when a consumer asks') was about the ADVERTISED MENU, which the ruling deletes. What survives is smaller and simpler: the SAMPLER reads cpu today; memory/disk join the reading when a consumer reads them. No menu, no mounting.

(b) DEAD 2026-08-04 — level-vs-edge triggering and unsubscribe were the SUBSCRIPTION's semantics. There are no subscriptions. BaseShim already answers both for every probe in the system (a poke per crossing, `while_true` to opt back into per-pulse, `gathered_enough` to retire) — which is itself evidence the broker was duplicating the shim.
(c) DEAD 2026-08-04 — 'express advertise/subscribe as bus messages' has nothing left to express.
(d) the real host sampler (rich per-core CPU, memory, disk) is the OS-specific backing this device will own — a thin edge; the predicate physics is proven by injection
(e) sudo_relay (privilege) is a host service in this same family, built standalone first — it migrates behind this abstraction when a second consumer makes the seam pay

(f) the line-crossing/POKE emit (the flake-adjacent event) is NOT yet instrumented: the poke fires in BaseShim._fire (the shim is the diagnostic RECEIVER, not an emitter) and level eval is per-pulse (a firehose); a device-side fire-hook or edge-detection grows when a real flake needs watching. subscribe (rare, low-frequency) is the one clean device-side gate today
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_system_rackmount.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RESHAPED 2026-08-04 by the shim-routes-everything ruling; clauses (1) and (3) named the broker's own physics and died with it. RED, by physics, on any of: (1) THE DEVICE HOLDS ANOTHER DEVICE'S PREDICATE — any subscription table, probe menu, advertise/subscribe surface, or resolve-a-caller's-method indirection is the broker growing back, and the broker is what the ruling deleted; (2) a device somewhere fires a host-resource watch through anything other than its OWN shim (a second firing path is the defect, not a convenience); (3) the sampler leaks the OS into a caller — a consumer that has to know load-average-vs-/proc has lost the one thing this device is for; (4) the device pokes ANYONE itself rather than through its shim on the heartbeat pulse (re-absorbing the firing the shim owns), or re-grows a central scheduler / a trigger-kind enum; (5) `SystemRackmountDevice`/`SystemRackmountShim` stop subclassing `BaseDevice`/`BaseShim` / drop CP1-CP6, or `introspect()` stops reporting intention → state → settings in order.
how_it_learns: Yes. (1) The subscriptions + the pokes ARE the learning substrate: the device's state() surfaces who is waiting on which line (never the reading), and every poke is a why-bearing record on the bus — a threshold that never fires and one that fires constantly are both signals in the record, not in silence. (2) Law-6-local-evaluation is itself a learning stance: by keeping the host's data home and exporting only the wake-up, the system learns which host predicates it actually needs to advertise (cpu first, memory/disk as consumers ask) without ever coupling a consumer to the metric — the same start-narrow-and-let-evidence-widen discipline as sudo_relay's box. Its own horizon: the advertised menu (cpu today) and the level-triggered semantics are best-guesses-with-an-expiry — they firm up as real consumers (an ops device, the harvester, a memory-pressure watcher) subscribe.

owner: CC owns the system_rackmount code + its proofs and gates writes to them. The system device OWNS the host-resource data it serves predicates on; that data is never exported, only pokes are — the owner-gate for host metrics, made physics.
proof: proofs/test_system_rackmount.py — it advertises the cpu_threshold menu and refuses an unadvertised name; end to end through the heartbeat, 'alert me at 80% CPU' pokes the subscriber's feed when over the line and no one when under, with the raw reading (95) crossing the bus nowhere (Law 6); the scheduler goof is gone (no service/scheduler API, no enum); device-hood + shim-hood + Form v0 #2 order. Composes the heartbeat + the real bus (db_domain) + the shim + the Probe. Green bare (python3) and under the tester. FLAKE FOUND + FIXED 2026-07-22 (a learning specimen, Law 8): the Law-6 leak-check scanned the WHOLE envelope for the reading '95', including the bus-assigned random uuid `id` — which contains the hex substring '95' ~12% of the time, so the proof went red ~2/8 by pure chance (a verdict decided by a coin toss, exactly what Law 8 forbids). Measured, not guessed: reproduced 2/8 under concurrency, the failing envelope's body was clean and the '95' sat in the uuid; the check now scopes to device-authored fields (excludes the transport-assigned id/date). Re-proven 0 red over 96 concurrent runs. The 'silent red' was a harness artifact (the earlier loop did not surface the subprocess stderr); under the tester the AssertionError was always captured.
provenance: RULED 2026-08-04 (CairnCommons/decisions/2026-08-04-the-shim-routes-everything.json). Akien, on being shown the phrase 'system_rackmount already owns host-resource predicates': 'each device should own it's own everything as much as possible, that's encapsulation. SO RULED.' — and the positive half, which is the larger claim: the shim already interfaces the bus to the device it knows, so it should route EVERYTHING for that device, 'not even just messages'. So this device is the identity-correction TWICE: first from scheduler to owner (2026-07-18), now from owner-of-predicates to owner-of-the-READING. The pattern in the miss is worth keeping: from a true premise (the host has one owner) I built a registration protocol so other devices could park their predicates here, when the encapsulation I was reaching for was one line of code in their own shims. Born 2026-07-18. First built (mislabeled) as `cairn/rack/` — a 'rack' that was actually a trigger-firing scheduler; then re-homed as a SchedulerService under a service-abstraction framing (cairn 5cb593a). The design conversation with Akien (evening) corrected the model twice over: the rack is the chassis (bus + shims), and the system rackmount is not a scheduler at all but the SYSTEM DEVICE — the owner of host-resource predicates, serving threshold probes through the universal heartbeat + shim + bus. Reworked to that shape (built last in the heartbeat+probe+bus rework, composing every piece before it); the SchedulerService + trigger-kind enum deleted. A specimen of learning-its-gates: the identity was corrected by the owner before it hardened, and the code caught up to the corrected intention. Next: the spine resumes (MAP.md:892) — inference domain → web server.
